question: Let \[ \begin{aligned} T={}&\frac1{3-\sqrt8} -\frac1{\sqrt8-\sqrt7}\\ &+\frac1{\sqrt7-\sqrt6} -\frac1{\sqrt6-\sqrt5}\\ &+\frac1{\sqrt5-2}; \end{aligned} \] then
solution:
Each denominator is the difference of square roots of consecutive integers. Multiplying by the corresponding sum makes the denominator equal to \(1\). For \(k=5,6,7,8,9\), the denominator is positive, and
\[
\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}-\sqrt{k-1}}
=\frac{\sqrt{k}+\sqrt{k-1}}{k-(k-1)}
=\sqrt{k}+\sqrt{k-1}.
\]
Applying this identity gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
T={}&(3+\sqrt8)-(\sqrt8+\sqrt7)\\
&+(\sqrt7+\sqrt6)-(\sqrt6+\sqrt5)\\
&+(\sqrt5+2).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every interior radical appears once with each sign, so \(T=3+2=5\). Thus \(T>2\), and the answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
